links.passage: Soil water tension is closely related to plant stress, and crop yield and quality are closely related to SWT irrigation criteria (Shock et al., 2007b).
supporting_passages: In these conditions, irrigation scheduling based on soil water tension can be directly related to plant performance.
The use of a soil water tension measuring device provides a continuous measurement analogous to the force (suction) necessary to extract water from the soil.
links.inference_note: The preceding sentences establish that the SWT irrigation criteria are obtained with a soil water tension measuring device, and the cited sentence ties those criteria to crop yield and quality.
reference_entries: Shock, C.C., A.B. Pereira, B.R. Hanson, and M.D. Cahn. 2007b. Vegetable irrigation, p. 535–606. In: Lescano, R. and R. Sojka (eds.). Irrigation of agricultural crops. 2nd Ed. Agron. Monogr. 30. ASA, CSSA, and SSSA, Madison, WI.

links.passage: Phene and Beale (1976) grew sweet corn (Zea mays) at 10, 20, and 40 kPa measured 15 cm below corn plants with tape, furrow, and sprinkler irrigation systems on sandy soil on the coastal plains of South Carolina.
supporting_passages: They sought to provide water and nutrients with the porous tube and minimize nutrient loss.
Sweet corn yields did not differ between SWT irrigation criteria or irrigation systems, but less water was required and less nitrate was leached with tape.
links.inference_note: The citation sits in the first sentence describing the trial with drip tape (porous tube), and the later sentence states that less water was required with tape than with furrow or sprinkler.
reference_entries: Phene, C.J. and O.W. Beale. 1976. High-frequency irrigation management for water and nutrient management in humid regions. Soil Sci. Soc. Amer. J. 40:430–436.

links.passage: Hybrid poplar tree (Populus deltoides · P. nigra) growth was measured with variable SWT on silt loam in semiarid eastern Oregon (Shock et al., 2002a).
supporting_passages: Rooting was mostly in the 0- to 30-cm layer and SWT was measured with granular matrix sensors at 20-cm depth.
Growth was favored by an irrigation criterion of 25 kPa compared with 50 and 75 kPa.
links.inference_note: The cited study scheduled irrigation by SWT measured with granular matrix sensors, and the following sentence states that growth was favored by the 25 kPa criterion.
reference_entries: Shock, C.C., E.B.G. Feibert, M. Seddigh, and L.D. Saunders. 2002a. Water requirements and growth of irrigated hybrid poplar in a semi-arid environment in eastern Oregon. West. J. Appl. For. 17:46–53.

links.passage: Richards et al. (1962) grew ‘Haas’ avocado (Persea americana) near Riverside, CA, with sprinkler irrigations initiated at 50, 100, and 1000 kPa.
supporting_passages: Tensiometers and gypsum blocks were placed at 0.3-m depth and at distances of 0.6 to 1.2 m from the tree trunk depending on tree size.
Tree trunk growth was greater with irrigations at 50 kPa.
links.inference_note: The cited trial used tensiometers and gypsum blocks to set the SWT irrigation criteria, and the later sentence states that tree trunk growth was greater at the 50 kPa criterion.
reference_entries: Richards, S.J., J.E. Warneke, and F.T. Bingham. 1962. Avocado tree growth in response to irrigation. Calif. Avocado Soc. 1962 Yearbook 46:83–87. 15 Nov. 2010. <http://www.avocadosource.com/CAS_Yearbooks/CAS_46_1962/CAS_1962_PG_83-87.pdf>.

links.passage: Serrano et al. (1992) grew strawberries in coastal Catalonia, Spain, at criteria of 10, 30, 50, and 70 kPa under drip irrigation.
supporting_passages: The SWT was determined by the average of tensiometers at 10- and 20-cm depth and placed 15 cm from a drip emitter.
Total strawberry yield and fruit per plant were greatest at 10 to 30 kPa.
Average fruit size was greatest at 10 kPa.
links.inference_note: The cited trial scheduled irrigation by tensiometer-measured SWT criteria, and the later sentences state that yield, fruit number and fruit size were greatest at the wetter criteria.
reference_entries: Serrano, L., X. Carbonell, R. Savé, O. Marfà, and J. Peñuelas. 1992. Effects of irrigation regimes on the yield and water use of strawberry. Irrig. Sci. 13:45–48.

links.passage: Using tensiometers, Oki et al. (1995) demonstrated that smaller irrigations at wetter SWT criteria resulted in greater rose productivity.
reference_entries: Oki, L.R., J.H. Leith, and S. Tjosvold. 1995. Tensiometer-based irrigation of cut-flower roses. 1994 Project report to the Calif. Cut-flower Commission.
links.section: Flower production and ornamental plants in nurseries

links.passage: Leith and Burger (1989) automated tensiometers to control greenhouse irrigations and were able to improve chrysanthemum (Chrysanthemum ·morifolium) production with criteria of 1.5 and 3.5 kPa compared with slightly drier criteria.
reference_entries: Leith, J.H. and D.W. Burger. 1989. Growth of chrysanthemum using an irrigation system controlled by soil moisture tension. J. Amer. Soc. Hort. Sci. 114:387–392.
links.section: Flower production and ornamental plants in nurseries

links.passage: Recently the viticulturist of Camalie Vineyards, Napa, CA, demonstrated the usefulness of SWT data for the production of quality grapes on clay (Holler, 2008).
supporting_passages: The SWT measurements were made using granular matrix sensors at 30- and 60-cm depths.
In the conditions of this vineyard, Holler determined that an irrigation criterion of 150 kPa at 60 cm was closely related to stem water potentials known to optimize grape yield and quality.
links.inference_note: The cited SWT data were obtained with granular matrix sensors, and the following sentences state that the resulting irrigation criterion optimized grape yield and quality.
reference_entries: Holler, M. 2008. High density, multiple depth, wireless soil moisture tension measurements for irrigation management. Camalie Networks, Napa, CA. 8 Nov. 2010. <http://66.82.73.54/High%20Density,%20Multiple%20Depth,%20Wireless%20Soil%20Moisture.pdf>.
links.section: Wine grapes and other examples of regulated deficit irrigation

links.passage: Recently the viticulturist of Camalie Vineyards, Napa, CA, demonstrated the usefulness of SWT data for the production of quality grapes on clay (Holler, 2008).
supporting_passages: The SWT measurements were made using granular matrix sensors at 30- and 60-cm depths.
Delaying irrigation until the soil reached 150 kPa resulted in water savings.
links.inference_note: The cited SWT data came from granular matrix sensors, and a later sentence states that delaying irrigation until the sensed 150 kPa threshold produced water savings.
reference_entries: Holler, M. 2008. High density, multiple depth, wireless soil moisture tension measurements for irrigation management. Camalie Networks, Napa, CA. 8 Nov. 2010. <http://66.82.73.54/High%20Density,%20Multiple%20Depth,%20Wireless%20Soil%20Moisture.pdf>.

links.passage: The combination of irrigation scheduling by SWT and careful management of well-designed irrigation systems can lead to highly efficient nitrogen fertilizer and water use (Feibert et al., 1998; Leith and Burger, 1989; Shock et al., 2004).
supporting_passages: The existence of precise measurement of SWT in itself does not imply that irrigation water use will be optimized or that the off-site negative effects of leaching or runoff will be minimized.
However, SWT measurements do allow these possibilities.
links.inference_note: The preceding paragraph frames the claim in terms of precise SWT measurement, so the efficient water use attributed to scheduling by SWT rests on in-field soil water tension sensing.
links.citation_in_text: Feibert et al., 1998; Leith and Burger, 1989; Shock et al., 2004
reference_entries: Feibert, E.B.G., C.C. Shock, and L.D. Saunders. 1998. Nitrogen fertilizer requirements of potatoes using carefully scheduled sprinkler irrigation. HortScience 32:262–265.

links.passage: Trials conducted in low rainfall environments demonstrated that irrigation in modest increments based on SWT plus rainfall closely matched the theoretical crop water demand based on estimated crop evapotranspiration (ETc) (Feibert et al., 1998; Shock et al., 1998b, 2000a, 2004, 2009).
supporting_passages: However, SWT measurements do allow these possibilities.

The combination of irrigation scheduling by SWT and careful management of well-designed irrigation systems can lead to highly efficient nitrogen fertilizer and water use (Feibert et al., 1998; Leith and Burger, 1989; Shock et al., 2004).
links.inference_note: The section ties irrigation based on SWT measurements to efficient water use, and this passage states that SWT-based irrigation increments closely matched crop water demand.
